'''BearOnline''' was the main studio responsible for operating several popular services on CatWeb, such as [[BLOX19]], [[HorizonsOS]], and prior to its shut down, [[Awoo]]. 

== History ==
BearOnline was originally established days after the release of HorizonsNexus, it was created to organize all of Calbear's services into 1 major studio, BearOnline later absorbed [[Awoo]] in early 2026.

=== Early History ===
In the beginning, BearOnline acquired [[HorizonsOS]] & [[Awoo]] and worked strictly on them, creating the popular HorizonsMusic platform, moderating Awoo, and managing HZN Services; however, in January 2026 the studio began development on a new product named [[BLOX19]]. The platform released in early beta on January 7th, 2026.

=== Late History ===
In july 2026, BearOnline annouced on discord they would be closing their services due to being unhappy with the moderation. they were muted and their annoucement was deleted, 2 days later on July 18th they posted a notice saying 

==== "BearOnline: Shutdown notice ====
Hey everyone. I'd like to notify you all that BearOnline will be shutting down. here is a complete list of services that will be closing soon: 
BLOX19, HorizonsOS (Online Features), and the BearOnline Blog. other products will not be shutdown because they don't feature any online features. Your data from our online services will be saved through cookies incase of an eventual return. (Decals have been archived which may result in visual mishaps.)

Thank you for supporting BearOnline ❤️ (Shutting down July 20th) "

The notice obviously lacks any information regarding why it shutdown, but the deleted post obviously states unhappiness with the moderation. Despite this, various APIs such as BearOnline Ads, & Mep Connect still operate.

== Services ==
BearOnline offers a variety of services such as:

* Calbear Ads (API)
* Mep Connect (API)
* BLOX19 
* BLOX19 Studio (Unreleased)
* HorizonsOS 
* HorizonsNexus
* HorizonsAccount (Unreleased)

=== Discontinued ===

* Awoo (Discontinued)
* HorizonsAero (Unsupported)
* HZN Services
* Calbear Emulator 

BearOnline no longer supports these services, and does not take suggestions, or feedback.

== CatWeb Rules (Website's Content) ==
CatWeb allows you to create website, share your work, and interact with others. These guidelines ensure a fun and respectful experience for everyone.

=== Content you make available on CatWeb ===
This can include sites you create or anything that you make available to others in CatWeb. They must follow Roblox's Terms of Use and their Community Standard. You remain responsible for the content you create with CatWeb. We do not endorse or approve user-generated content.

=== Sites you create ===
The websites you create within CatWeb should be respectful for other users. Avoid content that is hateful, discriminatory, or offensive.

'''You cannot create sites which:'''

* Impersonate CatWeb or other entities to try to mislead players.
* Use Donations in a malicious way to scam other players.
* Abuse exploits or otherwise bugs in the editor or its API.
* Include political content
* Include flashing images, rapid transactions, or loud sounds that could trigger epileptic seizures or discomfort, unless there is a clear, prominent warning displayed before users encounter such content.

=== How you use CatWeb ===
Do not create accounts for the purpose of acquiring domains for free.

=== CatWeb's paid services ===
In the event of a ban, you will not be eligible for refunds for any purchases or transactions made within the game.

When you purchase items or services within CatWeb, you acknowledge and agree that all sales are final and that refunds will not be provided in the event of a ban due to violations of our rules.

=== Site removal and actions ===
If your site is found to contain content that violates our rules, we may take actions to remove it from CatWeb. In this case, we will notify you via a ban message when you join the game.

If your site is mistakenly removed from CatWeb due to an error on our part, you have the opportunity to request a site recovery within 14 days of the removal.

After the 14-day period has elapsed, site removals become <u>irreversible.</u>

We reserve the right to suspend or terminate your access to CatWeb without prior notice if you engage in behavior that violates our rules.

== CatWeb User-to-User Communication Rules ==
Roblox's guidelines regarding chat features impact the ability for CatWeb creators to add said features to their website.

Broadcasts must not be used to create chats or allow user-to-user communication via custom messages.

The following rules apply to anyone using Broadcast scripting actions in their site.

=== User-to-User Communication ===
Anything that allows user to communicate to other users via custom messages is considered a chat feature.

Pre-set messages are not affected by this rule, as they are not user-generated and thus not custom messages.

=== Limitations and actions ===
If your site is found to contain user-to-user communication as defined above, we may limit it from using Broadcast actions.

You are able to appeal this decision and your site will be reinstated once you remove user-to-user communication, as defined above.<center>

CatWeb Scripting:
== About ==
'''CatWeb Scripting''' was a website hosted on the CatWeb platform that focused on providing scripts and code resources for users. The site served as a repository where users could access various scripts designed to add features, automate tasks, or modify the behavior of websites and online tools. These scripts were typically shared for educational purposes, experimentation, or integration into personal projects.

The platform aimed to make scripting resources more accessible to members of the CatWeb community by offering a centralized location for script distribution and discussion. Users of the site were often interested in programming, customization, and web development within the CatWeb ecosystem. Over time, CatWeb Scripting became known among some CatWeb users as a place to find and share scripts related to the platform.

== The Ban ==
'''CatWeb Scripting''' was a website hosted on the CatWeb platform that was later banned due to the inclusion of copyrighted material distributed without authorization. According to reports from CatWeb moderators, the site contained content that violated the platform’s policies regarding copyright infringement. After reviewing the situation and confirming the presence of the copyrighted material, moderators imposed restrictions on the site and eventually removed or banned it from the platform in order to comply with copyright rules and platform guidelines.

The copyright owner of the material reportedly took action after discovering the unauthorized distribution of their work on CatWeb Scripting. This contributed to the moderation decision and the enforcement measures taken by CatWeb. As a result, the site was no longer permitted to operate on the platform.

Following the ban and shutdown of the project, the owner of CatWeb Scripting reportedly experienced emotional distress related to the loss of the website and the consequences of the copyright violation.

Users go through a process to claim a spot:

# Mention the spot number they want to claim, for example, "Spot 37".
# Mention their site's URL (unless they only have one site).
# Optionally type the Image ID they want to use for their spot, or decide how the spot should be designed.

If the user doesn't provide an image ID or specific spot design, the background and color is decided based on the contents of their website.

== Layers ==
Once all 50 spots have been claimed, it will be saved as a '''completed layer''' and will be archived at '''archive.claimaspot.rbx'''. Spots can be "replaced" through this feature (once per layer).

== Archive ==
The archive has been added on 17 May 2025, when Layer 1 was completed. It shows every layer that has been completed, and their completion date.

A '''[[File:Rounded Corner.png|20x20px]] Corner''' in Roblox terms is called a "UI Corner." A UI Corner rounds out a GUI object to your liking. The table property you see is called the scale. The first number inside this is how big the roundness will be on the scaled direction, meaning if you set it to 1, it will always be rounded completely on at least one side. The second number you see is kind of like the first number, however, it revolves around uses pixels as a number, meaning it may not always be accurate.

For example, if you use a UI Corner and set the scale to {1,0} the UI Object would always be rounded. However, if you change it to a scale like {1,100} and the UI Object uses a scaled size value, a player with a bigger screen may not see it the same as a player with a smaller screen.

Datastore:
Datastore is an extremely advanced portion of the [[Script|scripting]] section. It is an add on task to perform setting or saving a player's data. Traditional datastore uses a permanent value that is always available. This is one of the key things of datastore, it can assign this permanent value to anything just like Roblox's system can.

== Setting data ==
For starters, doing both of these tasks are complex, so it is best recommended to be looking at the scripting page before reading this. Anyways, to load data, we need two values: a variable and cookie. These are going to be set later so set the cookie to "user_id" if you follow the later example. Before even getting the cookie, later we will use the user's ID to save it, meaning we need to use the user ID function to set it as well. So, we will first use the "Get local user ID > _" function. This allows the scripter to get the player's user ID seamlessly. Now that we have the user ID, we can set the data. To do this, we will use the "Set _ to _" function. This allows us to get our cookie that is saved previously. Now, on your own, you should be able to decipher whatever you put into the cookie when setting it and set it to your own values. In the end, it should look something like this: 
 { When website loaded...

 Get local user ID > user_id

 Get {user_id} > cookie

 }

== Saving data ==
To save data, we first need two values, a variable and a cookie. So, what's a cookie? A cookie is the uniform ID of the cookie. This means we probably don't want to set it to a random number, otherwise we will have problems with setting the data. The "Get _ to _" can do this function described, but again, we need those two variables. So, you may be thinking "This seems impossible." However, it is an extremely easy task to perform, just hard to understand. To set these two variables, you want to get the User ID with "Get local user ID > _." This variable name can be set to anything, but this variable must not be changed at all. The user ID is unique to one player, this means we can use it to set the cookie ID. This should look something like this:
  { When website loaded...

 Get local user ID > user_id

 Set {user_id} to {any}

 }
In this example, the {any} could really be anything. However, I would recommend putting a table inside the {any} value so you can assign multiple things to one cookie. Also, I wouldn't bother with increasing the cookie at all, this function is practically useless as you would almost never use it. The delete cookie function is the same as well, except you may use it to save bytes. This concludes saving our data. 

== Conclusion with normal datastore ==
In the complete version, you should have something like this, I will use a table as an example. None of these variables actually work or do anything, that is up for you to do:
  { When website loaded...

 Get local user ID > user_id

 Get cookie {user_id} > cookie

 Set variable ifcookie to "false" -- setting variables --

 Set variable clicks to 0

 Set variable timesClicks to ""

 Set variable string to ""

 Set variable timesJoined to 0 -- done setting variables, now on to getting data --

 Iterate through {cookie} ({index},{value})

     If {index} is equal to 1

         Set variable {clicks} to {value}

     If {index} is equal to 2

         Set variable {string} to {value}

     If {index} is equal to 3

         Set variable {timesClicks} to {value}

     If {index} is equal to 4

         Set variable {timesJoined} to {value} -- variables are now set to their desired values using index --

 Repeat Forever -- minimize data loss even if the player is kicked --

     Create table dataTable

     Set entry 1 of dataTable to {clicks} -- variables will be saved --

     Set entry 2 of dataTable to {string} -- variables will be saved --

     Set entry 3 of dataTable to {timesClicks} -- variables will be saved --

     Set entry 4 of dataTable to {timesJoined}-- variables will be saved --

     Wait 0.1 seconds -- ensure that the frame rate is still stable --

 } 

== Reinforced data systems ==
What are reinforced data systems?  Reinforced data systems check if the cookie does not exist, leading to no errors saying something like "You tried to index nil with variable," meaning that the cookie doesn't exist. '''Discover''' is another local CatWeb website (URL = "catweb://discover") that you can visit by clicking the "Discover" [[button]] in the new tab, or typing the URL "catweb://discover" in the "Search or type a URL" top bar below the tabs section located at the top of your screen.

''Discover'' shows a list of websites you can visit created by other players in the server. You can view the description of the websites, as well as the icon. There is an option for '''I'm feeling Lucky''', which takes you to absolute random website ''<small>(fixed: not from the list)</small>''.

I'm feeling Lucky has recently been removed and replaced with the website with the most visits (aka the first one in the list of websites)

== Sort Order ==
It is sorted based on visits, but with some exceptions. (This is why you normally see pages with at least a few hundred visits)

While this sounds unfair to new websites, CatWeb has looked at that problem. Websites that are new will be ranked higher than websites that are months old with the same number of visits.

Websites can also be ranked higher by updating, and CatWeb includes a label for it being popular, recently updated, or new. Making your website more engaging and making people stay longer will not bring your website up the discover page. Since there is no cooldown between visits, this situation can be abused by repeatedly redirecting to the same URL over and over. However, I suggest you should not try to make your website redirect to itself over and over, as that could get your site deleted or suspended.

{{Website1|webname=dreamverse|screenshot1=DreamverseLogo.png|caption-screenshot1=The social game that does not break any rules!|url=dreamverse|owner=@blue46g|visits=103|purpose=Multiplayer game}}

Dreamverse is a 2D Online MMO-like game created by @blue46g to fuse the concepts of Club Penguin and [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rec_Room_(video_game) Rec Room] into one game without breaking any rules, the game has Moderated UGC, Dreamverse Originals and so much more.

== Early History ==
The project came to be when owner @blue46g (also known as of the deckard on discord) thought of making a social hangout game that did not break any of the new rules imposed by roblox (the April 2026 preset chat nuke) so he made dreamverse, A game that is keeping the same feeling from before the nuke with moderated UGC but still following the rules.

== DreamNet ==
DreamNet is the central web portal for dreamverse, where you can view the following: Photos, Profiles, What people are doing and even change your Profile Picture without opening the game!

== Dreamverse Studio ==
Dreamverse Studio is the second option for creating games on Dreamverse, it is a Out-Of-Client option or OOC which means it is not on the same page as the game client unless it needs something there then it can.

== DreamScript ==
DreamScript is Dreamverse's scripting language designed to make it so that more things can be published onto dreamverse (ex. a obby with moving platforms) A script in dreamscript for a moving platform is the following:

function testidk[] (

objects.clone.ObjectName(xparam, yparam)

results.poll.PrevLine()

loops.forever{

objects.tween.ObjectName(xparam, yparam, style, time)

objects.tween.ObjectName(xparamdiff, yparamdiff, style, time)

}

)

== Datastoring Incident ==
Sometime in September 2026, Datastoring the datastore provider for Dreamverse ended up getting stuck by the catweb limit hammer causing all datastoring services to cease and BLUE46G to no longer be able to access the panel nor data he would say that since the game needed datastoring to work to store accounts, rooms and other data he could only work on tiny snippets of Dreamverse Studio, this also made it so the Creator could not work on user profiles on DreamNet.

== Updates ==

'''Beta Testing (August 12th):'''

Dreamverse opened up its Beta Testing access to [[Sillyfun]] and [[VFX]] on August 12th.

'''Scripting (August 27th):'''

On August 27th, dreamverse revealed that it was working on a scripting language called DreamScript which compiles to Catweb's way of doing Luau, games using DreamScript can be made with Dreamverse Studio.

'''Release soon? (August 29th):'''

On August 29th, the owner of dreamverse said that it is ready to release, he just needs to fix some stuff first.

Elevate:
'''Warning! This wiki contains spoilers for the elevate franchise!'''

Elevate is a franchise by [[Mayor]]. The games (except 3 and 4) have you play as a elevator worker who replaced the original. You can do tasks and meet new creatures. There are currently 5 games in the franchise (4 and 5 unreleased).

'''Elevate 1'''

In Elevate 1, you start as a new elevator worker, you meet some creatures once you first enter the elevator. Next, you enter the first floor where you meet Firehand and is given a task to press the button. Firehand explains that the old elevator worker would be mean and abusive towards them and that they and the other creatures will give you a chance. You go press the button once you finish talking with Firehand. After all that, you take the elevator and end up on the second floor. Your new task is to grab the wrench which is not hard to find. If you click it you immediately get stopped by a creature named Error. Error introduces himself and explains that he set traps for the old elevator worker. He then proceeds to grab the wrench for you and you leave the floor. As you take the elevator to the third floor, the elevator becomes broken and you have a new task, fix the elevator. After you fix it, everything goes back to normal and you enter the third floor. There, you meet Deva and Capybar. Your next task is to find missing wires for the elevator. If you talk to Deva first, she will explain Capybar has what you're looking for. Capybar will give you the wires and you go to the fourth floor. On the fourth floor, you meet someone named Tyba but you also must enter the control panel room. Tyba explains that she turned ugly because of the old elevator worker. She then explains the control panel is behind her but her message gets tagged (Mayor states that he did it on purpose for humor). You then are allowed to enter the control panel and go to the fifth floor. On the fifth floor, you don't meet a creature but rather the old elevator worker. You then get trapped on a rope and the old elevator worker tries getting his job back. Capybar comes and rescues you. Afterwards, you end up in a boss fight with the old elevator worker. If you lose, game over. If you win, you beat the game.

== Games ==

Here, you can play Tic-Tac-Toe with someone else, or a bot (still a work in progress).

=== Snake ===
'''Link:''' games.rbx/snake

This is a singleplayer game where you navigate a snake to get food (represented with an apple) by pressing the arrow keys. The snake gets longer each time an apple is eaten. The snake cannot run into itself or any edge of the map, otherwise the game is over. The top right of the game window shows your high score and current score. A recreation of the popular video game Tetris, where you drop sets of blocks and try to form a full horizontal line to clear it. The system for placing blocks is slightly different from the one used in actual Tetris. The right of the game window shows the next piece, current level, your score, amount of lines cleared and your high score. The leaderboard shows the top 3 highest scores. There is also a D-pad in the bottom-left of the screen for mobile support.

It allows you to create group chats, known as “parties”. It was created September 6, 2025. 

== Features ==

=== Parties ===
Parties are the name of group chats in hParty. Party messages can only be seen by people in that specific party.[[File:Hparty ui.png|thumb|360x360px|An example of a hParty party.]]

=== Invites ===
The site has an Invite feature that allows you to invite your friends to pages without publicly sending the code in a chat. When you are invited, you will have the option to Join (takes you to the code) or Decline (removes the invite popup). To invite someone, they must be on the homepage or in a party and you must be in a party. You need to type their username to invite them.

=== Short links ===
hParty allows you to generate short links using the prt.rbx service, that is on the bottom of every hParty. It will show you prt.rbx/Your Code, so while in code 123 it would generate prt.rbx/123, of which simply redirects you to hparty.rbx/party?code=123.

hParty is also testing using invite.rbx for the same purpose as the other service, prt.rbx. Invite.rbx is less likely to tag when sent.

== Community usage ==
hParty, while allowing group chatting with friends, has also gained a role as a community chatting site. As you can change the code to anything, this allows you to create custom codes for your own site. For example, [[7he]] has a hParty link to the hParty code “7herbx”.

== Attach and hParty copies ==
hParty was previously rivals with Attach after @mixmillys (who is now banned), the creator of Attach, said it was a copy. They later collaborated. Additionally, hParty caused many other Party sites to emerge, most infamously FlameConnect (previously FlameParty). FlameConnect was later shutdown and now both FlameConnect and FlameParty redirect to hParty.

== Word combination feature ==
For a few days, hParty allowed you to combine words (which also caused some inappropriate chat messages), but the rules to User-to-User Communication were later updated, forcing 7he to put the site in maintenance for a few days.

After the site returned, the word combination feature was removed and it now uses normal presets.{{DEFAULTSORT:hParty}}

{{Event|event-name=Halloween Event + Update|start-time=Sunday, October 26, 2025, 5:00 PM|end-time=Sunday, November 9, 2025, 5:00 PM|event-description=🎃 CatWeb Halloween Event + Update is releasing on October 26th!

- Learn more on hallway.rbx|event-thumb=Hallway Event Thumbnail.png|caption-event-thumb=The event thumbnail.}}

'''Hallway''' was the event dedicated to Halloween 2025.  The event released on '''October''' '''26/27 2025''', along with the '''v2.14.0.0''' update. The event could be played at '''catweb://hallway''', which could also be accessed from the '''[[Settings]]''' page.

== Information ==

=== Intro ===
When going to '''catweb://hallway''', you would see an elevator and text saying "The room is quiet and empty. Click the elevator to begin." Once the elevator is clicked, an intro sequence made up of text starts playing during the loading screen.

"You approach the Hallway: an endless strech filled with doors."

"Behind each door could be anything: a treat, a surprise..."

"...or maybe something that takes your candy. 🤫"

"Almost there..."

"Welcome to Hallway, [USER DISPLAY NAME]!"

You are then prompted to click the first door. You can then press the arrows on the sides of the page view different doors.

=== Behind the doors ===
When knocking on any door, one of these things could happen:

==== Candy ====
The door will open and reveal a single piece of candy. Clicking it grants you 1 candy, which is added to the counter in the top right. The candy's color is randomized.

==== Winning Smile ====
The door will open and reveal a "Winning Smile" face filled with TV static. After a bit, it steals 1-3 candy from your counter and says "i took your halloween candy". The only way to prevent winning smiles from taking your candy is by using the '''Candy Bucket''' item. You can also decrease the amount with the '''Luck Potion'''.

==== Jar ====
A jar on top of a table can be seen when the door is opened. When clicked, it gives 1-3 cookies which need to be clicked for them to be added to your counter. Sometimes, the jar will be empty and not provide any cookies, deeming the door useless.

==== Wheel ====
A spinnable wheel appears which can be clicked. Whatever the arrow on the right lands on is what will happen. You could gain candy, lose them through Winning Smiles, or gain cookies. The '''Luck Potion''' can increase the chances of getting good spins.

==== Potion Shop ====
A shop will appear with music playing the background, and two potions: a '''Luck Potion''' for 15 cookies and a '''Speed Potion''' for 20 cookies.

==== Backdoor ====
Going through this door takes you a random amount of doors ahead in the hallway.

==== No Response ====
The door will not open and text appears saying "No response..."

=== Non-door rooms ===
The following rooms don't have doors.

==== Shop ====
This is a different kind of shop compared to the '''Potion Shop'''. Clicking it will show the two items it sells: '''Mystery Chocolate''' for 15 cookies, and a '''Candy Bucket''' for 25 cookies.

==== Door 1,000 ====
This door is required to get the badge for this event, titled "The End?". It takes the appearance of a black background with a yellow glow. Once you reach 20 candies and click on this door, you will earn the badge and an ending sequence will play.

=== Items ===
Throughout the hallway, you can get items from shops. There are four different items that can be collected.

==== Luck Potion ====
These can be bought from '''Potion Shops''' for 15 cookies. They decrease the amount of candy taken from Winning Smiles, increase luck on wheels, and increases luck when using the '''Mystery Chocolate'''. The potion effect lasts 3 minutes.

==== Speed Potion ====
These are also sold at '''Potion Shops''' for 20 cookies. Clicking the arrows to move through the hallway becomes a little faster. Like the '''Luck Potion''', its potion effect lasts 3 minutes.

==== Mystery Chocolate ====
These are sold at normal '''Shops''' for 15 cookies. They can reward the player candies, take them away through the winning smile, or reward the player cookies.

==== Candy Bucket ====
Also sold at normal '''Shops''', they cost 25 cookies and can prevent the winning smiles from taking your candies 3 times. This applies to normal winning smile rooms AND wheels. Additionally, when a wheel rolls a double winning smile, it will count as 1 use instead of 2.

== Badge ==
{{Badge|badgename=The End?|description=Reach Door 1000 with 20 candy in the 2025 Halloween event, Hallway!|id=2646727277176711|badgeimage=The End? Badge.png}}
Upon reaching door 1,000 with 20 candies, you would receive a badge titled "'''The End?'''". An end sequence made up of text will then play, showing your stats, like how many candies or cookies you have collected, how many you lost, the colour of the last candy you collected, etc.

'''HorizonsOS''' (Formerly stylized as "horizonsOS") is a CatWeb website developed by [[BearOnline|BearOnline Studios]]. It is mostly known for its Windows Aero based design.

== Versions ==
HorizonsOS operates like Windows, and aims to release a major version every once-in-a while.

=== HorizonsAero ===
HorizonsAero was the original release of HorizonsOS. It is based on the OpenHorizons kernel, it lost support around February 2026; few months after its November 2025 release.

=== HorizonsNext (Scrapped) ===
HorizonsNext was a scrapped version of HorizonsOS, it was inspired by Windows 8 and used a similar "metro" UI design, though, it was ultimately scrapped due to "Major Re-evaluations" within [[BearOnline]].

=== HorizonsNexus ===
HorizonsNexus is the second release of HorizonsOS. Like its predecessor, it was based on OpenHorizons and, as of writing, it is still officially supported. It reused assets from the scrapped HorizonsNext OS, and HorizonsAero.

== Trivia ==

* It is often credited as the first OS on CatWeb to function without redirecting to new pages for every app, instead displaying apps in windows, wit the exception of few apps, though, these apps are refered to as FSA (Full-Screened-Applications) and are often this way to save resources on the main desktop.

The '''[[File:Image_Icon.png|20x20px]]''' '''Image''' element is an [[:Category:Elements|element]] which displays an '''[[File:Image_Icon.png|20x20px]] Image'''. === Copying an Image ID ===
To copy an '''Image''' '''ID''' manually without searching for an image in the Image Finder/Searcher, You'll have to go to a real browser (Google Chrome, Safari, Firefox, etc.), and go to the [https://create.roblox.com/store/decals Roblox Decals Creator Marketplace], Go to the image you like and you'll see the URL at the top. Double click the random numbers (aka the ID) that's surrounded with "/asset/", and the other slash with the name of the Image/Decal, and do '''CTRL + C''' and then go to Catweb again and '''CTRL + V''' to paste it in the "Image" property, Example in this image:

== Pages ==

=== /captcha ===
Subpage with ''CUFMOU'' (Checking the user for the means of use). Initially, the subpage was intended for captcha, but it had to be changed, since there are no bots in CatWeb. Here you can check the user's device for your site. This is a useful feature if you need it when a player wants to play a game.

After the '''styron.rbx/captcha''' address, specify the return parameter (?return=your site link) with the link of your site. Then you get the output with the parameters ''device'' (pc or mobile) and ''time'' (duration of verification).

=== /math-play ===
A subpage with a simple multiplication table game. After you complete 10 examples, you will see a window with your result. The offer will change depending on the time.

FOR ADMINS: if you need to, please set the article to protected. thank you. - RetroBloxxer{{Information about something :D|title1=List|image1=List.png|type=Styling Element|caption-image1=The icon featured in CatWeb.}}

A list is an styling element that groups every element thats parented to something in a specific order.

List properties include:

* Padding 
* Sorting Order 
* Wrap
* Direction
* Vertical / Horizontal Alignment

=== Details about List properties ===

==== Padding ====
Padding is the spacing between each elements on the list based on the Y and X axis. For example, if you do the padding 0,10 , the elements will have a 10 meter (i think) spacing.

==== Sorting Order ====
Sorting the order has 2 options. Name and layout order.

Layout order is based on the element order of every list elements. For example, if you add a text that says "hi" before another text that says "hello", the text saying "hi" will be the first on the list order.

Name is based on the elements names. For example, if you name a element 1 and name another 2, the element named 1 will come first. You can use the F2 keybind to rename the selected element.

==== Wrap ====
Wrap basically prevents elements from going out of bounds.

==== Direction ====
The direction of the list elements. If you do it vertical, it does the order vertically. If horizontally, it does the order horizontally.

==== Alignment ====
The alignment of the list elements. 

Horizontal alignment esentially puts the order to the left, center or right of the element in the current line.

Vertical alignment esentially puts the order to the top, center and bottom of the element.

'''LiveChat''' is a now defunct chatting site created by '''[[creeper_pug]]''' (@pugwares) on 26 July 2024. The site shut down on '''30 April 2025''' due to the new [https://catweb.fandom.com/wiki/CatWeb_Rules#CatWeb_User-to-User_Communication_Rules '''policies regarding user-to-user communication''']. It now redirects to '''live.rbx?l=defunct''', which includes a "learn more" button that shows why LiveChat shut down.

== Versions ==
'''LiveChat''' had 4 (5 if you count DeadChat) major versions, listed below:

=== Bagels | The Chat Room (v0) ===
LiveChat was originally hosted on '''bagels.rbx'''. It wasn't even named LiveChat during this time. Only the most recent 4 messages would be displayed. There was also a donation button on the bottom right, and text on the top left stating the chat cooldown is 5 seconds long.

Site: '''misc.bagels.rbx/chat'''

=== LiveChat (v1) ===
The name '''LiveChat''' would be suggested by someone using the chat on Bagels. You could mute users, play music, and more. The donation animation would also make its first appearance.

Site: '''livechat.rbx/v1'''

=== LiveChat (v2) ===
This version was made to compete with other chatting sites, and therefore had a refreshed UI. It had image chat, shorthands like {lenny} and {kirby}, a documentation, and allowed the user to mute up to 3 users at once.

Site: '''livechat.rbx/v2'''

=== LiveChat (v3) ===
This is the current version of LiveChat. It can be laggy due to the donation animation. You could connect your '''POPic''' account to set the background music, profile picture, and more. A lot of features have also been revamped, like the muting system. Themes were also added as a paid feature.

Site: '''livechat.rbx''' or '''livechat.rbx/v3''' (this version cannot be accessed)

=== DeadChat ===
'''DeadChat''' simply included a grave, tracking the amount of time '''LiveChat''' has been defunct for. The favicon was a greyed out version of '''LiveChat v3'''<nowiki/>'s favicon. It would also play random sounds in the background.

Site: '''deadchat.rbx'''

== Trivia ==

* Since LiveChat didn't censor numbers, it was used as an alternative way to send image IDs.

== Mips Icons ==
'''mips-icons.rbx''' is a highly popular utility and resource website. Serving as the largest dedicated icon library. It is an essential tool for CatWeb developers, designers, and scripters who want to improve the user interface of their websites. 
{{Website1|webname=Mips Icons|screenshot1=https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/1373673799693635625/1515869422705967205/image_98dp_E3E3E3_FILL0_wght400_GRAD0_opsz48.png?ex=6a3092e9&is=6a2f4169&hm=c4d59a420edb6d558647c69b1ab7b0e159f4c57905569f82e5c851fd64243103&=&format=webp&quality=lossless&wi|caption-screenshot1=Icon from Google Icons|url=mips-icons.rbx|creation_date=March 30, 2026|owner=Mips (Tollie_Mips)|visits=1000+}}

=== Overview ===
Before the creation of mips-icons.rbx, developers in CatWeb often struggled to find clean, uniform images for their website buttons, navigation bars, and social links. '''mips-icons.rbx''' solved this by compiling a massive, easy-to-search database of icons specifically formatted for the game's website editor.

Currently boasting over '''400 icons''' the library is constantly expanding. The site developers frequently tease upcoming updates, promising new batches of icons based on community requests.

=== Features and Usage ===
The website functions as a visual catalog. When players visit `mips-icons.rbx`, they are greeted with a sleek UI where they can browse different icon sets.

==== To use an icon from the library, a player typically follows these steps: ====

# Search for the desired icon on '''mips-icons.rbx''' (e.g., "Home button," "Shopping Cart," "Play icon").
# Click on the icon to generate its specific image ID or direct integration link.
# Open their own site in the CatWeb Editor.
# Paste the ID into an image frame.

=== Popular Categories ===
The library is divided into several main categories to help developers navigate the massive collection:

* UI Essentials: Hamburger menus, search magnifying glasses, home buttons, and settings gears.
* Social & Media: Icons mimicking popular real-world and in-game platforms (like SearchGo).
* E-Commerce: Shopping carts, Robux coin symbols, and checkout checkmarks for donation pages.
* Cursors & Pointers: Custom pointers to make site navigation feel unique.

=== Trivia ===

* It is widely considered a "must-bookmark" site for anyone serious about building top-tier sites in CatWeb.
* Passing the 400-icon milestone was a major event for the site, cementing its status as the absolute largest visual asset library.

Network Blocks:
== Information ==
[[File:Network blocks.png|thumb|Networking blocks category]]
'''Networking Blocks''' or '''Broadcasts''' are a category of blocks. The blocks allow to broadcast something across a website, for example you could make a working chat system. They also have their own trigger, '''When message received'''.

Recently, CatWeb has added cross-site broadcasts, allowing you to communicate through lots of sites. The extra parameter is the domain the message was received from, so if you get unwanted broadcasts, you can filter them easily.

== IMPORTANT! ==
Broadcasts should not be used for making chat features (features where you can type your message or arrange your message, but not ones where you pick a choice to send a message)

==List of blocks==
The blocks are as following:

* '''Broadcast''' <message> '''across page'''
* '''Broadcast''' <message> '''across site'''
* '''Get local username →''' <variable>
* '''Get local display name →''' <variable>
* '''Get local user ID →''' <variable>


== Fun facts ==
These are facts found by the fans in-game, by either digging further in the code (exploiters smh), or the ones which found it the hard way, or just reading [https://catwebtemplates.com/limits CatWeb's Limits].
* Broadcasts have a ping of 120 - 170 ms.

* Sending broadcasts too quickly could hit a rate limit of 5 per 2 seconds (2.5/s), pausing all broadcasts from being pushed. The 5/2s applies to the entire site. However, if you use uncached cross-site broadcasts, the limit is 4 per 20 seconds (that is 1 per 5 seconds).

ROISHSITE is a platform that replicates Roblox in 2011, not completely but isn't supposed to. It currently has 2 versions with mutiple sites and sits at around 4k combined visits.

The first version of ROISHSITE, before was called just ROISHSITE. It wasn't too functional and rarely gets updates.

Created and owned by '''PACMANDJA''', the site focuses on recreating the user experience and interface of Roblox from the 2015–2017 era. It is notable for its deep integration with external CatWeb systems and its rare origin story. '''Site Information''' * '''Domain:''' roogledev.rbx * '''Creator:''' PACMANDJA * '''Status:''' Active * '''Theme:''' 2016-2017 Roblox Nostalgia * '''Categories:''' Revival, Utility, and Multi-Device '''Technical Features''' * '''z4 Account Integration:''' RoogleDev features a functional login API. Users who are logged into their '''z4.rbx''' account will see their specific username (e.g., '''DanteNov17''') and real-time avatar thumbnail automatically loaded into the site's profile elements. * '''Multi-Platform Gateway:''' The site uses a "Device Detection" landing page that allows users to manually select their hardware for an optimized layout. '''Interfaces''' '''1. Landing Page''' The initial gateway where users choose between '''TV/Console''' or '''Other Devices'''. It features the classic red-outline Roblox logo and a minimalist selection menu. '''2. Computer & Mobile Mode''' Designed for mouse and vertical-touch navigation. * '''Side Navigation:''' Features a sleek black sidebar with white icons for '''Home, Catalog, Avatar, and Settings'''. * '''Dynamic Layout:''' Displays a "Recently Played" carousel and a top-aligned profile header with a functional refresh button. = Roblox PC™ (RoPC) =
'''RoPC''' (anagram for '''Roblox PC''') is an online virtual machine (VM) platform created by '''[https://catweb.fandom.com/wiki/koliemini Koliemini]'''. Powered by '''NODE OS.''' allowing users to experience a desktop‑like environment directly through Roblox.

== The Purpose of Roblox PC ==
Our purpose is to serve as an '''online virtual computer within CatWeb''', created for players who want to explore and experience '''recreated versions of classic Windows operating systems'''. By simulating environments from '''Windows 7, Windows 10, and Windows 11''', Roblox PC offers:

* '''Nostalgia and preservation''' – bringing back the look and feel of older Windows systems in a playable form.

* '''Learning and exploration''' – allowing users to interact with desktop workflows inside Roblox without needing the actual hardware.

* '''Customization and creativity''' – giving players the freedom to personalize their virtual OS with themes, fonts, and layouts.

* '''One Experience for all devices''' – bringing ideas to make devices smarter for our ecosystem.

* '''Community connection''' – designed to encourage sharing, collaboration, and digital publishing projects.

=== Features ===

* '''Mayura AI''' – An AI companion built into Roblox PC, powered by the Roblox PC Cloud and managed by Ace. It provides assistance, guidance, and interactive support for users inside the virtual environment.

* '''Drag n’ Drop Feature''' – Enables seamless image transfer from one device to another, making publishing and sharing easier.

* '''Dynamic Animations''' – Fluid animations applied to clicks and transitions, creating a smooth and engaging user experience.

* '''Advanced Technology''' – Powered by the Roblox PC Cloud Database and handled by Ace. It enriches viewing habits with advanced learning technology.

* '''Glass 7 Design''' – A clean, simple, and prestigious unified experience, built on the new Glass 7 design language.

[[File:BloxClub_Icon.png|thumb|132x132px]]

=== BloxClub™ Subscription ===
Designed to unlock advanced tools and personalization options for players. It enhances the virtual computer experience by providing exclusive features beyond the standard environment.

=== What's Included on this Plan? ===

* '''Personalization''' – Unlocks free access to themes, and layout customization for your virtual OS.

* '''AI Integration''' – Expands the capabilities of Mayura AI, offering smarter assistance and deeper interaction inside Roblox PC.

* '''Shared Plans''' – Allows multiple users to collaborate under one subscription, enabling family or team access.

* '''Exclusive Tools''' – Provides early access to advanced technology features powered by the Roblox PC Cloud.

(BloxClub Subscription Costs 60 Robux as a One-Time Purchase. If you cleared your cookies or got your Subscription cookie corrupted, please make a report on '''[https://www.roblox.com/games/start?placeId=16855862021&launchData=ropc.rbx/feedback ropc.rbx/feedback]''' instead of purchasing the same product all over again. '''We will automatically re-activate your subscription once your report is valid'''.)

=== What makes Roblox PC Superior? ===
Roblox PC is designed to give users a complete and reliable experience that feels both modern and authentic. Its strength comes from combining advanced technology with a simple, prestigious design language. The Glass 7 interface ensures everything looks unified and professional, while dynamic animations make every interaction smooth and engaging.

The platform is powered by the Roblox PC Cloud Database, managed by Ace, which keeps performance seamless and responsive. Built‑in Mayura AI provides intelligent assistance, helping users navigate and personalize their environment with ease. Features like Drag n’ Drop make sharing and publishing effortless, while personalization options allow users to shape their workspace to match their style.

Most importantly, Roblox PC respects its users with a fair subscription model. Once you’ve joined, your benefits remain secure, and if technical issues like cookie expiration occur, the system offers a transparent re‑activation process instead of forcing extra payments. This commitment to fairness and usability is what makes Roblox PC stand out as the superior choice.

=== Misconceptions on our platform ===
Some people assume '''Roblox PC''' and '''[https://catweb.fandom.com/wiki/SearchGo Search Go]''' are identical because they use similar engines. In reality, they are separate projects with their own goals, features, and identities. Sharing a technical foundation does not mean one copies the other — Roblox PC was built independently and offers its own unique design, subscription model, and user experience.
[[File:Node_OS_Logo.png|thumb]]

== About our platform ==
Roblox PC runs on its own upgraded operating system called '''NODE OS 7'''. This system was developed specifically for Roblox PC to deliver a lightweight yet powerful foundation. NODE OS 7 introduces the new '''Glass 7 Design''', which brings a clean and unified look across the entire platform. It also enhances '''light transparency''' and '''animations''', making the interface smoother and more visually engaging.

Because NODE OS 7 is built by Roblox PC itself, it is optimized for performance and efficiency, ensuring that users enjoy a responsive environment without unnecessary overhead. This operating system is what makes Roblox PC feel modern, polished, and distinct from other platforms.

=== "One Experience for all Devices" ===
This represents the mission of NODE OS 7 — to deliver a consistent, unified environment across every type of hardware. Whether you’re on a laptop, phone, or even a TV, NODE OS adapts seamlessly while keeping the platform lightweight, and secure.

This approach shows how Roblox PC keeps innovating, ensuring that no matter what device you use, the experience feels familiar, lightweight, and connected. It’s about bringing the same superior performance and design everywhere, without compromise.

== History ==

=== 2024 — Original SCL.RBX ===
SCL.RBX was created on '''July 13, 2024''', by '''[[newmedal]]'''.

The original SCL.RBX was created as a recreation of the Roblox website within CatWeb. During its early development, SCL became a relatively low-quality recreation of Roblox that relied on the '''RoPro''' and '''BTRoblox''' Chrome extensions for additional functionality.

The original SCL established the foundation for the project's later development.

=== Late 2024 — SCL2.RBX ===
In late 2024, [[newmedal]] continued development of SCL by creating '''SCL2.RBX'''.

SCL2.RBX was essentially '''SCL 2.0''' and continued the original SCL project under a new domain. It was not intended to become a completely separate brand from SCL.

The Roblox recreation continued to be developed while [[newmedal]] also began working on a separate Creator Hub.

=== Early 2025 — Creator Hub ===
In early 2025, '''create.scl2.rbx''' was introduced as the SCL Creator Hub.

The Creator Hub was designed to work alongside the Roblox recreation. Similar to the real Roblox website, pressing the '''Create''' button on the Roblox recreation would take users to the Creator Hub.

During this period, SCL consisted of two connected experiences:

* '''scl2.rbx''' — The Roblox recreation
* '''create.scl2.rbx''' — The Creator Hub

=== 2025 — Creator Hub Becomes Main Focus ===
Throughout 2025, development gradually shifted toward the Creator Hub.

The Creator Hub became the main focus of SCL development. A web card was provided on the Creator Hub allowing users to visit the Roblox recreation at '''scl2.rbx'''.

The Roblox recreation was still being worked on, but development had become very limited compared to the Creator Hub.

=== Early 2026 — Development Break ===
In early 2026, [[newmedal]] took a long break from SCL development.

During this period, active development of the Creator Hub largely stopped.

=== Mid 2026 — Return to Development ===
[[newmedal]] returned to SCL in mid-2026 and resumed development.

The Creator Hub was fixed up and improved, with development once again focusing on improving its interface and functionality.

=== 2026 — Transition to Community ===
Approximately two months after returning to development, [[newmedal]] discontinued the Creator Hub as the primary direction of SCL.

Development then transitioned toward '''community.scl2.rbx'''.

The transition marked a shift from the Creator Hub-focused era of SCL toward a community-focused project.

The former Creator Hub at '''create.scl2.rbx''' was not completely abandoned. It can still be accessed through a button on community.scl2.rbx for users who miss the Creator Hub or prefer its experience.

== Roblox Recreation ==
The Roblox recreation was one of the earliest parts of SCL.

It began with the original SCL.RBX recreation in 2024 and continued through SCL2.RBX.

As development shifted toward the Creator Hub in 2025, the Roblox recreation received increasingly less development.

In 2026, development of the Roblox recreation was discontinued and the recreation was eventually shut down.

The Roblox recreation was later released as an '''open-source project''', allowing others to use, modify, and experiment with it.

The shutdown of the Roblox recreation did not mark the end of SCL.

== SCL2.RBX ==
'''SCL2.RBX''' was introduced in late 2024 as SCL 2.0.

Despite the SCL2 name, it was primarily a continuation of the original SCL project rather than a completely separate brand.

[[newmedal]] rarely refers to the project as "SCL2" and generally continues to use the '''SCL''' name.

The SCL2.RBX domain was used to continue the SCL project after the original 2024 SCL.RBX recreation.

== create.scl2.rbx ==
'''create.scl2.rbx''' was the SCL Creator Hub.

It was introduced in early 2025 and eventually became the main focus of SCL development.

The Creator Hub was designed to work alongside the Roblox recreation, with the recreation's '''Create''' button directing users to it.

Although the Creator Hub was later discontinued as the primary direction of SCL, it remains accessible through a button on '''community.scl2.rbx'''.

== community.scl2.rbx ==
'''community.scl2.rbx''' is the community-focused continuation of the SCL2 domain.

It became the direction of SCL after the Creator Hub was discontinued in 2026.

The platform also provides users with access to the former Creator Hub through a dedicated button.

== Name and Branding ==
The name '''SCL2''' was primarily used to represent the continuation of SCL after the original 2024 version.

SCL2 was not intended to replace the SCL identity. [[newmedal]] generally continued referring to the project as '''SCL''' and rarely used "SCL2" when discussing the project.

The SCL2 domain therefore became another part of the broader '''SCL legacy'''.

'''Script Basics'''

Script Basics for every category of blocks.

This is a full tutorial for making your first ever working site! Many people have been using all this info or similar to make awesome websites! You can do that too by following this tutorial!

"//" is a comment

If you know luau, then it will be easy to make a website

== Data Types ==
Data types are the types of data that the computer  or programming language can work on. Here are the luau data types that are compatible with CatWeb:

* nil - Stands for nothing, is basically a variable without anything. You can leave the input blank for nil.
* number - Is a data type that uses numbers. <number>
* string - Is a data type that uses text, symbols numbers and more. <string>
* table - Is a table data type. It uses dictionaries. More info on dictionaries [https://create.roblox.com/docs/tutorials/fundamentals/coding-5/intro-to-dictionaries here] <nowiki><table></nowiki>
* object - Is an object data type. <object>
* function - Is a function data type. <function>
* cookie - Is a cookie data type. More info on Web Cookies [[Cookies|here]].
* variable - Is a data type that is a pointer to data. More info on variables [https://catweb.fandom.com/wiki/Script_Basics#Variables below].

== Events ==
Events are what trigger your code to function. Examples are

* when website loaded - Triggers code inside to run when website loaded
* when button pressed - Triggers code inside to run when button pressed
For example...<syntaxhighlight line="1" start="1">
when website loaded
   // Code below will execute when the website is loaded
   
when <button> pressed
   // Code below will execute when the button is pressed
</syntaxhighlight>

== Console ==
These blocks enable you to debug your site like any other programming language.

=== Blocks ===

* Log - Logs a message into the console.
* Warn - Logs a warning message into the console.
* Error - Logs a error message into the console, and stops further script execution.

=== Examples ===
This script outputs "Hello World"<syntaxhighlight line="1" start="1">When website loaded
   Log (Hello World)
   // Output - "Hello World"</syntaxhighlight>

This script outputs "Example warning." in yellow text.<syntaxhighlight>
when website loaded
   warn (Example warning)
   // Outputs "Example warning" in yellow text.
</syntaxhighlight>This script outputs "Example error." in red text and stops further execution on the script.<syntaxhighlight>
when website loaded
   error (Example error)
   log (Example)
   // Outputs "Example error" in red only and does not log "Example".
</syntaxhighlight>

== Looks ==
Looks are blocks that change the looks of your website. You can set an object visible or invisible, or set a property to an object.

=== Blocks ===
Most of the blocks in the Looks section are self-explanatory. I will only list some that people struggle to understand.

==== Set <property> of <object> to <any> ====
This block can set any property of an object to any value. Some of the supported properties are:

===== Any Webrenderer Object =====

* Background Color
* Background Transparency
* Visible

=== Examples ===
'''Make Visible/Invisble Script'''

[[File:My image for info 1.png|thumb|348x348px]]

<syntaxhighlight line="1">

when (button) pressed
  make (object) visible
  // or
  make (object) invisible
</syntaxhighlight>

'''Set Object Color When Pressed'''

<syntaxhighlight line="1">
when (button) pressed
 set (Background Color) of (object) to (any)
 // You can put in any hex color like #fffff
</syntaxhighlight>

'''Set Object Text When Pressed'''

<syntaxhighlight line="1">
when (button) pressed
 set (object) text to <any>
 // Put in any text  Note that some text will be filtered/tagged.
</syntaxhighlight>


'''Delete Object when pressed'''

<syntaxhighlight line="1">
when (button) pressed
 delete (object)
</syntaxhighlight>

== Variables ==
A variable is a value which points to data in your memory. You can store values like numbers, strings, tables, etc on variables. The variable name is the string pointer to the data in the memory. More info on roblox luau variables [https://create.roblox.com/docs/luau/variables here]

'''Declaring A Variable'''

To declare a variable, all you need to do is to add a set variable to any block.<syntaxhighlight line="1">
When website loaded...
 set (variable name) to <any>
 // Set any and variable to anything you want
</syntaxhighlight>'''Using A Variable'''

To use a variable in <any>,

* For mobile, just use curly brackets and the variable name inside { (variable name) }
* For pc, there is a dropdown menu. Choose variable in the dropdown.

Both works in PC but only 1 works in mobile. Both works in both devices using <object> input type.

=== Variable Scopes ===
In the Mega Update (2.12) of CatWeb, it added scopes to variables. Scopes are the types of variables based on where they can be used. You can add a scope to a variable by adding a unique prefix to the variable name, ex. {l!myVariable}. Here are the all scopes of a variable:

* Global - This is the most popular scope and has no prefix. The variable can be used throughout all scripts in the page.
* Object - This has the "o!" prefix, and the variable can be only anywhere inside the script.
* Local - This has the "l!" prefix, and the variable can only be used inside the current thread or event. This can be used for temporary variables that will soon not be needed.

==== Examples ====
This prints the value of {myVariable}.<syntaxhighlight>
when website loaded
   set (myVariable) to (1)
   log ({myVariable})
   // Outputs/Logs the value of myVariable or 1.
</syntaxhighlight>
This will not print the variable because it is out of the scope.<syntaxhighlight>when website loaded
   set (l!myVariable) to (qwerty)
   
when website loaded
   wait(1)
   log({l!myVariable})
   // Will not log the variable because it is out of scope.</syntaxhighlight>

== Math ==
It is pretty self explanatory. Math blocks are blocks that do math.

=== Blocks ===
Some of the blocks are self explanatory so only blocks that people will have a hard time understanding.

==== Run math function ====
You might have heard of the math functions (sin cos tan). This is the block that will do most of them.

== Time ==
[[File:TimeCatweb.png|thumb|422x422px|Time Blocks]]
Time blocks are for calculating the current time using mostly the Unix Time. Unix Time are the seconds since the Unix epoch or January 1, 1970 at 00:00 UTC.

=== Time Blocks ===
 Get unix timestamp -> <variable>
This gets the Current Unix Timestamp into a variable
 Get server unix timestamp -> <variable>
This requests the Server to get the Unix Timestamp, yielding the code.
 Get tick -> <variable>
This gets the Current Unix Timestamp with ''decimals'' into a Variable.
 Get timezone -> <variable>
Gets the user's timezone in UTC, for example. -8:00 UTC, will return -8 and 8:00 UTC will return 8.

== Network ==
These blocks allow you to send or recieve data from other players. As the rule suggests, these blocks should not be used to make chat features. It is okay if you use pre set chat.

==== Custom themes ====
If you have [[File:PremiumIconRecreation.png|20px]]'''[[Premium|CatWeb Premium]]''', then you can make your own themes by changing the background color, text color and primary color. You can make up to 10 custom themes.

=== Accessibility ===
The '''Accessibility''' section includes settings for players with disabilities.

==== Saturation ====
This setting lets you decide how saturated ingame colors are. This does not effect user-generated websites nor images.

==== Visual Effects ====
These settings allow you to change how visual effects in CatWeb look. Currently, you can only stop or reduce CatWeb motion effects with '''Reduced Motion''', which you can also sync with your actual Roblox settings.

==== Contrast ====
This section has 1 setting, which enables higher color contrast where applicable.

=== Cookies ===
The '''Cookies''' section displays a list of every single site that stores information about you through [[File:Cookie.png|20px]][[Cookies|'''cookies''']]. The list is sorted alphabetically, from 0-9 then A-Z. Each row in the list shows a domain name, how much data is stored about you in that site (measured through bytes and kilobytes), and the amount of cookies stored on that site.

=== Chat ===
The '''Chat''' section allows you to configure settings about the chat window in the bottom right of your screen.

==== Show chat tag in chat ====
This is currently the only setting in the Chat section (as of v2.13.0.7). If you have any chat tags like the CatWeb Premium chat tag or chat tags from events, they can be disabled or enabled using this setting.

'''Symbolics.rbx'''<ref>Symbolics.com, created by Symbolics Inc. [https://symbolics.com]</ref> is a recreation of the first commercial domain name, symbolics.com. The site uses the original pre-2009 symbolics.com layout. It features a standard CatWeb white background and the original Symbolics logo.

* '''Macsyma Upgrade Special Offer:''' Located at `symbolics.rbx/macsymaspecial`. A flavor page referencing legacy support for Macsyma software, including mentions of CD-ROMs and physical documentation.

* The creator's username is hidden within the mailing address on the contact page.
* The "No More Age Check" notification is designed to mimic the Microsoft Edge popup style.

== Trivia ==
* The real Symbolics.com was the first .com domain ever registered.
* The site was launched on the exact same calendar day (March 15) as the original 1985 registration.
* The UI is an exact 1:1 match of the original site's layout.

== Templates ==
There are two types of templates, the first being actual templates that you can use in your site, the second type are templates that teach you CatWeb scripting concepts.

=== Actual Templates ===

==== Music ====
This template adds looped background music to your site.

==== Random Number ====
This template lets you generate a random number when a specific button on your site is pressed.

==== Timer ====
This template adds a timer to your site when it's loaded, letting you set any text label to display the timer.

=== Concept Templates ===

==== If Statements ====
This template teaches how If Statements. The script will set a test variable to "a", and check if that variable is equal to "a". Since they are equal, the site will log "Test is equal!"

==== Math & Variables ====
This template teaches how math functions and variables work. It starts by setting a test variable to 2, then multiplies the test variable by 2. Since 2 times 2 is equal to 4, the site will log "Test is now: 4!"

==== Date and Time ====
This template is a simple script that makes the site log the current day of the week, date, month, year and time.

==== Network ====
This template makes use of message broadcasting. It broadcasts a test message across the page, and logs "[MESSAGE SENDER] broadcasted: test!" This will be logged for everyone visiting the site.

== Facts ==

=== Facts ===
* An advertisement for [[luau.rbx]] was once the last option in the templates menu, but it disappeared after the website didn't update and became outdated after July 12. The devs added right-click functionality to action blocks probably because of this.

From [[Articles|articles.rbx]] ([[Lamb|@TheSecretLamb]])<ref>https://www.roblox.com/games/start?placeId=16855862021&launchData=articles.rbx/view?id=8</ref>

== What are backdoors? ==
Backdoors are hidden pieces of code hidden inside of a larger script that performs something <u>malicious</u> or something <u>without the users knowledge</u>, the most famous backdoor was the file.rbx backdoor where the text encoder could take control of sites.

== Backdoor ban ==
Since the recent outbreak of backdoors, the creator of CatWeb has stated that any more backdoors are now <u>punishable</u> by a permanent ban as they go against the roblox terms of service.

== Impact                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               ==
Since this new rule took place, games.rbx no longer has a backdoor rendering easyvisits.rbx pretty much useless and the backdoor on file.rbx is believed to be completely removed from the script allowing users to use it again without their websites being controlled by a third party.

== Is this the end of backdoors? ==
To enforce the backdoor ban, moderators would need to know about the backdoor but because some backdoors are usually hidden, the moderators may struggle finding the backdoors for a while, leading some sites to continue their backdoors. Please stay safe on CatWeb and only import something if you trust the creator.

'''Update 2.15''' or '''Collaboration Beta + Update''' is the 15th mega update in CatWeb 2.0 released in December 1, 2025. It adds the Collaborate (Beta) feature. 

== Additions/Changes ==

=== Collaborate (Beta) ===
You can now collaborate, with up to 10 people. This is a public beta, with the full collaboration release coming early next year.

=== Copy & Paste ===
Copy, cut and paste your elements anywhere instantly, across sites, pages or Collaboration sessions.

=== Mobile UI ===
It was now made easier to edit your sites and use CatWeb on mobile with several UI updates and performance improvements.

* The editor now opens more faster compared to before 2.15.
* The script editor is now more larger in mobile giving more room to edit your scripts.
* Up to 6 tabs appear on your phone, the rest available in tabs search.
* You can now pinch to zoom and use two fingers to pan when editing scripts in Mobile.

=== Increased Limitations ===
Do so much more with 5MB of variable data (prev 512 KB) (before mega update part 2 16 KB) and about 5 broadcasts per 2 seconds (2.5 broadcasts/sec) and around 900 bytes of broadcast data, with improvements to other features coming soon.

== Bug Fixes ==

* Resizing elements with Aspect Ratio constraint on is now less buggy.
* Fixed resizing rotated elements breaking.

== Trivia ==

* This might be the last update of 2025.
* Because this is Collaboration Beta, it is likely that there will be a better update to Collaboration in a future update.

== Services ==

=== Verto Works ===
'''Verto Works''' is a text editing site similar to '''Microsoft Word''', where you can type in some text and even decide a title for the document. After the compilation update, its' limit of text and saving is unlimited. It was 500 before.

=== Riffly ===
'''Riffly''' is a music player site similar to '''Roify''' or '''[[Listen]]''', where you can pick from a list of songs to play. These songs will not automatically stop playing when you click on another song, meaning you can have multiple songs playing at once. You'll have to manually click a button to stop all audio. Also, it provides an input field for a custom ID to play.

=== Random Number ===
'''Random Number''' is a simple random number generator that generates a random number between 1 and 100 (default) every time you reload the page or press the "Restart" button (which regenerates a number). You can also change the range of numbers.

=== Search ===
'''Verto Search''' is a simple search engine. You can search a site and it will show up, along with (the site name)1.

=== Clock ===
'''Clock''' is a simple clock that shows time in 12-hour format (example: 1:00 PM) along with AM/PM and date in DD.MM.YY format.

=== Random Image ===
Instantly generates a number in a special range to get a random image. If the image doesn't load there is a button to randomize the image again, and there's also a button to open this image in Image Viewer.

=== Random fact ===
Generates a random wacky fact or a random Verto fact, for example: A single day on Venus is almost longer than a whole year on Earth. 

=== MaliciousCheck ===
Checks to see if a site is unsafe. This tool is not fully reliable and it doesn't have all the information to check. Be aware that it won't list every website. It uses only links to check; it doesn't have a database of sites, but it has a database of keywords to mark it as malicious. It is not 100% accurate. Don't fully rely on it.

Entertainment service that allows guessing a number between 1 and 100 range.

Allows viewing an image similarly to asset.rbx, however has very few features compared to asset.rbx.

Shows current trending websites, although 0_080463 added "that's all trendings i've seen, i maybe missed some" meaning the page doesn't show all trending sites.

Generates a random color; for example: #1e4dd5. It also introduced verto.rbx/rdl, which stands for Redirect Dark/Light, it redirects to your preferenced theme (dark/light).

You can count a number (increase by 1 or decrease by 1) in this service. Introduced in the '''2 Services At The Same Time''' update.

== Stranger Cats ==
Inspired by "Stranger Things", Stranger Cats is a story where 3 cat friends play together when suddenly one of them goes missing. (We will call the Orange-Black cat "Bill", the jumping cat "Michael", and the orange cat  "Dusty".)
=== Ep 1. (Monster's Feast) ===
The trio is playing a board game and gets bored. Bill decides to go home, so Dusty prays on his downfall. Bill gets lost and a monster appears in front of him asking if he could eat him. Bill responds with "Yes" however it is apparently opposite day. Bill seemingly ends up eating the monster.
<hr>
=== Ep 2. (Upright) ===
Michael and Dusty meet up at school and wonder where their friend is. Meanwhile, Bill is wandering around the forest. He ends up finding a monster which tells him the dimension he is in at the moment is the "Upright" dimension, Bill asks him about the point of him being there, so the monster says that they were just bored. Bill questions why they say "we" and the monster reveals other monsters with him. Back to where Michael and Dusty are, they tell a black cat (We'll call them "Luca") that he is missing, and they respond with "great".
<hr>
=== Ep 3. (Another Day, Another Victim) ===
Bill is running away from the monsters. Meanwhile the other party is searching for Bill and finds his phone. Michael, Dusty, and Luca ask a scientist in the "freaky lab" on where Bill is. The scientist watches footage of last night and finds a scene of Bill eating the monster. The scientist however responds that they haven't found Bill. The three leave, and the scientist goes to the head's office. They tell them about how the monster ate Bill (which is confusing since Bill ate the monster.) At night, Michael is sleeping when suddenly a monster breaks into his room. It cuts to a black screen where he screams in terror.
<hr>
=== Ep 4. (The backstory) ===
The setting takes place in the "freaky lab" 3 Days before the incident. An alarm rings as monsters are trying to escape from their dimension. The scientists decide to send 2 people out to kill the monsters. The people however chicken out and don't want to go in. The monster climbs in however and eats them both as they scream in terror. The monsters escape the facility and into a parking lot.
<hr>
=== Ep 5. (The great idea) ===
Michael ends up in the Upright dimension and finds Bill. Dusty and Luca are wondering where Michael is when suddenly another black cat appears (we'll call them Elmer) and tells them they know where they are. They lead them to a portal to the upright. The three enter the portal and get sent to the dimension where Luca admits going in was a "dumb idea".
<hr>
== Cat Game ==
Cat game is inspired by the show "Squid Game" as cats fight for their lives and only their lives.
=== Ep 1. (Welcome to the Island) ===
A cat borrows money from a banker (We'll call the borrower Uni-Joheun) and the banker tells them to give it back soon. Uni-Joheun says ok and gambles it all. Unfortunately, he loses his money. The banker knocks him out and he wakes up in Cat Game.
<hr>
=== Ep 2. (Red light, Green light) ===
The banker reveals to be the host and says that the person to win will be able to go out free. Any who lose will die. The first game (Red light Green light) is played and 3 people die. One for tripping, another for making fun of one of them, and another for shouting "I've played these games before".
<hr>
=== Ep 3. (Tasty Cookies) ===
One contestant asks about them leaving the game, so the guards end up shooting them. The next game starts as one of the contestant immediately eats a cookie and dies. They decide to skip the game. Meanwhile, at the police station, a cop asks the sheriff if he should do anything about 456 people going missing. It is then revealed that the sheriff was bribed into encouraging no response.
<hr>
=== Ep 4. (The great reveal) ===
The cats play the next game "Tug-Of-War" as they battle for their lives with a rope. The right side ends up winning and the left loses. It then cuts to a scene where the banker is bribing one of the police officers. Luckily, one of the cops is spying on them and finds out about their tricks.
<hr>
== Outside In ==
Outside In is inspired by the movie "Inside Out". Emotion cats stand inside a cat's mind and control how the cat feels. The movie starts out with a cat asking another cat if they want to "go out". We'll call the cat asking the other one out "Maxwell". The cat they ask however says "uh no" and leaves. Inside Maxwell's mind, an anger and disgust cat react and say that it went horribly. Joy comes in, so they decide to throw her out the window due to her being "annoying". Sadness comes out too to find where joy is, so they decide to throw them out the window, too. Maxwell's comes home and their mom calls them "rude" after they said that school was good. Anger and disgust want to run away however Joy appears and knocks the two out.<hr>
== Five Cats At Freddy's ==
5 cats meet up in a pizzeria. They decide they should go explore an abandoned Pizzaria. They end up getting scared and leave. Suddenly, Bonnie is gone. One of the cats searches for them and dies. Chica goes missing, too. Another cat searches for them and dies. The cats get scared and decide to leave.<hr>
== Cat Note ==
The bell rings as a class scurries out. Suddenly, a notebook falls onto one of the cats outside and hits them in the head. They look at it and bring it home. The notebook is labelled "Cat Note" and the cat believes it must be a joke. They write that Mrs. Prudence dies from being eaten by another cat. It turns out that they do indeed die.

'''Yandex''' is a search engine created by '''Shiron''' (@ShironBros) on 29 June 2024. It provides a variety of different tools, mainly an alternative search engine, to the user. As of now, '''most of these tools cannot be accessed'''.

== Site design ==

=== Homepage ===
The homepage consists of a search bar, with 7 buttons on top for the tools. Below, it always displays that the temperature is 17° at night, and the user lives in '''Robloxia'''. Pressing '''Enter''' anywhere on the homepage, pressing the yellow "Search" button, or clicking one of the search suggestions (the last two require you to type in the search bar), will redirect you to the search page with the search query you entered.

=== Search page ===
The search page's layout is similar to most other web search engines like '''Google'''. On top is the search bar, which includes your search query and allows you to search more from there, and five tabs for '''Web''', '''Images''', '''Video''', '''Maps''', and '''Translate'''. Below are the actual search results. This includes a Yandex ad, a link to the website you searched, images (currently always the same), and two links at the bottom that do nothing (even though they are described as a link to Yandex). If the site you are searching for has been '''recognized by Yandex''', it's search result will include the site's favicon, name and description, and on the right, information about your site will be shown, and text at the bottom saying "'''Yandex GPT 5 Pro'''". If the site was not recognized, it displays a globe as the favicon, the search query as the site name, and the description "'''No information is available about this page'''"

== Yandex Tools ==
Yandex has 7 tools, however only one of them is available as of 10 May 2025, that being '''Yandex Metrica'''. It displays a box with your last Yandex search request since you loaded up Metrica, and the most searched websites (manually updated).
